sections.presenting_complaint: Pain below the right kneecap for 2 days.
sections.history: Gradual onset without specific injury; plays football (training three times a week plus matches) and school PE. Pain during and after sport and on kneeling. No night pain. No rest pain. No swelling, locking or giving way. No hip or thigh pain. No fever or weight loss. Limps only after matches. Older brother had Osgood-Schlatter disease at a similar age. No previous joint problems.
sections.medications_allergies: No regular medications. No known drug allergies. No asthma or peptic ulcer disease.
sections.examination: Tender bony prominence over the right tibial tuberosity. No knee effusion. X-ray of the knee normal. Full range of knee movement; ligaments stable. Both hips: full, pain-free range of movement. Normal gait.
sections.impression: Osgood-Schlatter disease of the right knee. No red flags.
sections.plan: Activity modification guided by pain. Ice for 15 minutes after sport. Paracetamol or ibuprofen 800 mg up to three times daily with food as needed. Refer to physiotherapy for quadriceps and hamstring stretching. Review if not settling in 6–8 weeks.
